Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment summary: Acute onset (few days) of dry, pruritic, red skin localized to hands and arms after swimming. No systemic symptoms (no fever, vomiting). Coconut butter applied for several days without improvement. Occupation (teacher) and family history of atopy noted. Clinician’s working diagnosis: dermatitis.
- Integration with DDx (consistent items):
  - Irritant contact dermatitis — High likelihood: supported by temporal relation to swimming, distribution on hands/arms, and occupational exposures (frequent handwashing/cleaning).
  - Allergic contact dermatitis — Moderate likelihood: supported by temporal association with swimming and recent topical coconut product use; delayed hypersensitivity possible.
  - Atopic dermatitis (adult-onset or flare) — Moderate likelihood: supported by family history of atopy and stress as a precipitant.
- Conflict noted: None significant between transcript and DDx; DDx suggestions align with history. (No contradictory clinical facts documented.)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Irritant contact dermatitis — High likelihood
  - Justification: Acute localized dry, red, itchy eruption on hands/arms after swimming; occupation implies frequent handwashing/chemical exposure; no systemic features.
- Allergic contact dermatitis — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Temporal association with swimming and recent topical coconut product use; localized pruritic dermatitis consistent with contact allergy.
- Atopic dermatitis (adult-onset or flare) — Moderate likelihood
  - Justification: Family history of atopy (asthma, hayfever) and recent stress may precipitate an atopic flare; presentation can be eczematous and pruritic.
